cases.question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.standalone_question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.answer_excerpt:
COMP 4537 (Internet Software Architecture) is a 3.0-credit course focused on the design, development, and management of web APIs. 

The course covers:
* What RESTful APIs are and why they matter.
* How HTTP and REST APIs relate to each other.
* CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations.
* The constraints of REST and the uses of HTTP status codes.

### Key Learning Outcomes
By the end of this course, you will be able to:
* Design and develop programs using REST, JSON, and HTTP.
* Design simple web services and secure backend API servers.
* Apply best practices, REST constraints, error handling, and HTTP status codes.
* Document and write specifications.
* Apply change management and versioning to designed APIs.

### Course Details
* **Prerequisites:** COMP 1537 and COMP 3522.
* **Program:** It is offered as a common course in Level 4 of the full-time Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma program.
* **Delivery:** 3 hours of lectures per week over 15 weeks (45 total hours).

Sources:
* https://www.bcit.ca/courses/internet-software-architecture-comp-4537/
* https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-systems-technology-diploma-full-time-5500dipma/
* https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261088086/

cases.question: What are the entrance requirements for the Computer Systems Technology diploma?
cases.standalone_question: What are the entrance requirements for the Computer Systems Technology diploma?
cases.answer_excerpt:
For the full-time Computer Systems Technology (CST) diploma, applicants must meet the program's entrance requirements, and applications are accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. 

While the specific high school course grades for the full-time CST diploma are not detailed in the available documents, the program offers a **Direct Entry** pathway for students who have completed equivalent coursework at BCIT or another institution and wish to enter directly into Level 2 or Level 3. 

To apply for Direct Entry, you must:
* Email cstdiploma@bcit.ca to request a pre-assessment information kit.
* Submit a completed pre-entry assessment approved by the program area.
* Provide proof of meeting all entrance requirements.
* Submit your complete application by July 15th for the Fall (September) intake, or by November 30th for the Winter (January) intake. 

*Note: If you enter the program via Direct Entry, you will not be eligible to apply for the Co-op program.*

If you are instead interested in the **Flexible Learning (Part-time) Computer Systems Diploma**, the entrance requirements are:
* **Post-secondary education:** Completion of the BCIT Computer Systems Certificate (CSC) program. You must be enrolled in or have completed your final term of the CSC before applying. 
* **English language proficiency:** Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent, which is met by completing COMM 110x in the CSC.

Sources:
* https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-systems-t

cases.question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.standalone_question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.answer_excerpt:
### BCITSA Health and Dental Plan Enrollment and Opt-Out

Yes, you are automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan if you meet the eligibility criteria, and you do have the option to opt out if you have alternative coverage.

#### 1) Automatic Enrollment
You are automatically enrolled in the plan if you are registered in a BCIT program designated as full-time that runs for **16 weeks or longer**. 
* The Student Association (SA) Health fee is automatically added to your tuition upon registration.
* Students in the International Student Entry Program (ISEP) or part-time/flexible learning programs are not eligible for this automatic enrollment.

#### 2) Opt-Out Process
You can opt out of the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan if you already have comparable extended health and dental benefits (such as coverage through a parent, spouse, or employer).
* **Deadline:** You must complete the opt-out process within **30 days from the start of your program**. 
* **Frequency:** This opt-out must be completed once every 12 months. 
* **Important Note:** After the 30-day deadline passes, opt-outs cannot be processed.

Sources:
* https://www.bcit.ca/admission/tuition-fees/full-time-studies/
* https://www.bcitsa.ca/student-services/health-dental/
* https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/medical-insurance/types-of-insurance/
* https://www.bcitsa.ca/about-us/student-fees/

cases.answer_excerpt:
### Entrance Requirements for the Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma

The specific entrance requirements for the full-time Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma are not in the available documents. 

However, if you are interested in the part-time (Flexible Learning) Computer Systems Diploma, the entrance requirements are:

*   **Post-Secondary Education:** Completion of the BCIT Computer Systems Certificate (CSC) program. You must be enrolled in or have completed your final term of the CSC before applying. If you completed the certificate more than five years ago, or have department-approved equivalent education, you may need to take additional courses.
*   **English Language Proficiency:** Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent, which is met by completing COMM 110x within the CSC.

Applicants for the part-time program are accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. 

To find the exact entrance requirements for the full-time CST program, please check the official BCIT website.

cases.answer_excerpt:
You have **30 days** from the start of your program to opt out of the BCITSA Student Health and Dental Plan. 

Please keep the following details in mind:

* The same 30-day deadline applies if you wish to add family members to your plan.

cases.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?
cases.follow_up: What TOEFL iBT score does Category 2 require?
cases.standalone_question: What TOEFL iBT score does BCIT English proficiency Category 2 require?

prior_turns.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?

cases.answer_excerpt:
To meet the Category 2 English language proficiency requirement using the TOEFL iBT, the required score depends on your test date:

*   **Prior to January 21, 2026:** You must achieve an overall score of **86**, with no section score less than **20**.
*   **As of January 21, 2026:** You must achieve an overall score of **4.5**, with minimum section scores of **3.5** in Speaking, Writing, Reading, and Listening.

The BCIT destination code for submitting your TOEFL iBT results is 9110. Please note that for assessment tests, your results must be dated no more than two years before your program's start date.

Sources:
* https://www.bcit.ca/admission/entrance-requirements/english-language-proficiency/
